translations.text: Paul, an apostle by the will of God, to the saints who are in Ephesus, and to the faithful through Christ Jesus:
Grace to you and peace from God our Father and our Lord Jesus Christ.
Blessed is God and the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who has blessed us with every spiritual blessing in the heavens through Christ.
Just as he chose us through him before the creation of the world, so that we might be holy and blameless before him in love.
He appointed us beforehand as children through Jesus Christ to himself, according to the good pleasure of his will,
for the praise of the glory of his grace, with which he has graced us through the Beloved,
through whom we have redemption by his blood and the forgiveness of our sins, according to the riches of his grace,
which he made to abound toward us with all wisdom and understanding.
He made known to us the mystery of his will according to his good pleasure, which he determined beforehand in him
for the ordering of the fullness of the times, to bring everything together under one head in Christ, what is in the heavens and on earth;
toward him, in whom we also were ordained and were appointed beforehand by the will of God, who made everything according to the counsel of his will,
so that we, who first hoped in Christ, should be to the praise of his glory.
through whom you also heard the word of truth, the gospel of your salvation, in which you also believed and were sealed with the Holy Spirit of promise,
who is the pledge of our inheritance, for the ransoming of our help, for the praise of his glory. 2.
For this reason I too, having heard of this faith of yours through the Lord Jesus and of the love that you have toward all the saints,
do not cease giving thanks for you; I make remembrance of you in my prayers,
so that God and the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the God of glory, may give you a spirit of wisdom and revelation in the knowledge of him,
and may enlighten the eyes of your heart, so that you may know what is the hope of his calling, and what is the wealth of the glory of his inheritance among the saints,
and what is the surpassing wealth of his power toward us who believe, according to the working of the strength of his might,
which he accomplished with Christ, for he raised him from the dead and seated him at his right hand in the heavens,
above all principalities and authorities and powers and dominions and every name that is named, not only in this world but also in the one to come.
And he subjected everything under his feet and gave him as ruler over all to the church,
which is his body, the fullness of him who has filled all things in all.
And you also, who were dead through your transgressions and sins,
in which you once walked according to the times of this world, according to the ruler of the authority of the air, the spirit that is now at work among the children of disobedience,
among whom we all also once conducted ourselves in the desires of our flesh, doing the will of the flesh and of the thoughts, and we were by nature children of wrath, just as the others.
But God, because he is rich in mercy, through his great love with which he loved us,
and because we were dead in sin, made us alive together with Christ, with Christ — by grace you are saved —
and raised us up together and seated us together in the heavens through Christ Jesus,
so that he might show in the times to come the surpassing riches of his grace, in kindness toward us through Christ Jesus.
For by grace you are saved through faith, and this is not from you, but is the gift of God:
not from works, so that no one may boast.
For we are his making, created through Christ Jesus for good works, which God prepared beforehand, so that we should walk in them.
Therefore remember that you were once Gentiles in the flesh, called the uncircumcised by those who are called the circumcision, which is in the flesh and made by hands,
For at that time you were without Christ, made strangers to the citizenship of Israel and strangers to the laws of the promises; you had no hope and were godless in the world.
But now through Christ Jesus you who were once far off have become near by the blood of Christ.
For he himself is our peace, who made both one and broke down the dividing wall of the barrier,
the enmity, by his flesh; he abolished the law of commandments by decree, so that he might create the two in himself as one new man, making peace,
and might reconcile both in the one flesh to God through the cross; he killed the enmity in it,
and he came and proclaimed the good news of peace to you, those far off, and to those near.
For through him we both have access in one Spirit to the Father.
From now on you are no longer strangers and sojourners, but fellow citizens of the saints and members of the household of God,
built on the foundation of the apostles and prophets, of which the head of its corners is Christ Jesus,
in whom the whole building, joined together, grows into a holy temple through the Lord,
on whom you too are built together into a dwelling place of God by the Spirit.
For this reason I, Paul, the prisoner of Christ Jesus for you Gentiles —
if indeed you have heard of the stewardship of the grace of God that was given to me for you,
for by revelation the mystery was made known to me, as I wrote to you before in brief,
by which you are able, when you read, to perceive my understanding in the mystery of Christ,
which was not revealed to another generation of the sons of men as it has now been revealed to his holy apostles, apostles and prophets, by the Holy Spirit:
that the Gentiles should be fellow heirs and of one body and sharers in the promise of God through Christ by the gospel,
of which I became a minister according to the gift of the grace of God given to me, according to the help of his power.
To me, the least of all the saints, this grace was given: to proclaim among the Gentiles the unsearchable riches of Christ.
and to enlighten all people as to what is the dispensation of the mystery hidden from the ages with God, who created all things through Jesus Christ,
so that the manifold wisdom of God may now be made known through the church to the principalities and powers of heaven,
according to the purpose of the ages, which he accomplished through Christ Jesus our Lord.
through whom we have boldness and access with hope through faith in him.
Therefore I ask that you not be grieved at my afflictions for your sake, which are your glory.
For this reason I bend my knees to the Father,
from whom all the families in the heavens and on earth are named,
that he may grant you, according to the riches of his glory, to be strengthened with power through his Spirit in the inner man,
so that Christ may dwell in your hearts through faith,
established and grounded in love, so that you may be able to comprehend with all the saints what is the breadth and length, the height and depth,
to know the love of Christ that surpasses knowledge, so that you may be filled with all the fullness of God.
Now to him who is able to do above all things, more than what we ask or know, according to the power of his help within us,
to him be glory in the church through Christ Jesus to all generations, forever and ever. Amen.
I, this prisoner in the Lord, beseech you to walk worthily of the calling with which you were called,
with all humility and gentleness, with long-suffering, bearing with one another in love,
striving to keep the unity of the Spirit by the bond of peace.
One body and one Spirit, just as you were called in the one hope of your calling;
one Lord, one faith, and one baptism;
one God and Father of all, who is above all and through all and in all.
but to each one of us grace has been given according to the measure of the gift of Christ.
Therefore it says: "He ascended on high and led captivity captive, and gave gifts to men."
But what does his "ascent" mean, if not this, that he first descended to the lower parts of the earth?
He who came down is the same one who was exalted above all the heavens, so that he might fill all things.
And he gave some as apostles, some as prophets, some as evangelists, some as shepherds and teachers,
for the establishing of the saints, for the work of ministry, for the building up of the body of Christ,
until we all attain to the unity of the faith and the knowledge of the Son of God, to a perfect man, to the measure of the stature of the fullness of Christ,
so that we may no longer be infant children, tossed by waves and carried about by every wind of teaching, by the craftiness of men and by cunning in the scheming of error,
but let us be true in love and make all things grow toward him who is the head, Christ,

from whom the whole body is joined together and made firm by every joint of supply, according to the help of the measure of each member; bring about the growth of the body for the building up of yourselves in love.
This therefore I say and testify before the Lord, that you must no longer walk as the other Gentiles walk, in the vanity of their mind,
darkened in heart, estranged from the life of God through the ignorance that is in them, through the blindness of their heart,
who have abandoned themselves and given themselves over to filthiness, to the practice of uncleanness in all greed.
But that is not how you learned Christ,
if indeed you have heard him and been taught about him, as the truth is in Jesus.
Put away from yourselves, as regards your former way of life, that old man, corrupted according to the desire of deception,
and be renewed in the spirit of your mind,
and put on the new man, created by God in righteousness and in the holiness of truth.
Therefore put away falsehood; let each of you speak the truth with his neighbour, for we are members of one another.
Be angry, and do not sin: do not let the sun go down on your wrath.
Nor give place to the devil.
Let the thief steal no more, but rather let him labor and do what is good with his own hands, so that he may have something to give to whoever is in need.
Let no foul word come out of your mouth, but only what is good for building up as the need requires, so that it may give grace to those who hear.
And do not grieve the Holy Spirit of God, by whom you were sealed for the day of redemption.
Let all bitterness and wrath and anger and shouting and slander be done away with among you, together with all wickedness.
Be kind to one another, merciful, forgiving one another, just as God has forgiven us through Christ.
Therefore be imitators of God, as beloved children,
And let us walk in love, just as Christ loved us and gave himself for us as an offering and sacrifice to God, for a fragrant aroma. (8)
But let fornication and all uncleanness or greed not even be named among you, as is fitting for saints.
And let there be no abomination and foolish talk or insolent jesting, which are not proper, but rather thanksgiving.
And know this, that every fornicator and unclean and greedy person, who is an idolater, has no inheritance in the kingdom of Christ and of God.
Let no one deceive you with empty words, for because of these things the wrath of God comes upon the children of disobedience.
Do not, then, become like them,
for you were once darkness, but now you are light through the Lord; as children of light, let us walk,
for the fruit of the Spirit is in all goodness, righteousness and truth.
Test what is pleasing to the Lord,
And have no share in those unfruitful works of darkness, but rather expose them.
For what is done by them in secret is abominable even to speak of.
But everything exposed by the light is made manifest, for everything made manifest is light,
for which reason it says: Awake, you who sleep, and arise from the dead, and Christ will give you light.
Take care, then, how you walk circumspectly, not as the foolish but as the wise;
redeem [?] the times, for the days are evil.
For this reason do not be foolish, but understand what the will of the Lord is.
And do not get drunk with wine, in which there is filthiness, but be filled with the Spirit.
Speak to yourselves with psalms and hymns and spiritual praises; sing to and praise God with your heart.
Give thanks always for all things in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ to God and the Father.
Submit to one another in the fear of Christ.
Wives, submit to your own husbands, as to the Lord.
For the husband is the head of the wife, as Christ is the head of the Church, and he himself is the Savior of the body.
But as the Church is subject to Christ, so also wives — to their own husbands in everything.
Husbands, love your wives, just as Christ loved the church and gave himself up for it,
that he might make it holy, and he cleansed it with that washing of water and with the word,
that he himself might present the Church to himself in glory, having no stain, nor fold of wrinkle [?], nor anything else of the kind, but that it might be holy and blameless.
In this way husbands ought to love their own wives, as their own bodies, for whoever loves his wife loves himself.
For no one ever hates himself, but nourishes and cherishes himself, as Christ does the Church,
for we are members of his body, of his flesh and of his bones.
For this reason a man shall leave his father and his mother and be joined to his wife, and the two of them shall be one flesh.
This mystery is great; but I speak concerning Christ and the Church.
Nevertheless you too, each one of you, love your own wife in this way, as yourself; and let the wife fear her husband.
Children, be obedient to your fathers and mothers in the Lord, for this is right.
Honour your father and your mother, which is the first commandment with a promise,
that it may be well with you, and that you may be long-lived upon the earth.
And fathers, do not provoke your children to anger, but bring them up in the instruction and teaching of the Lord.
Slaves, obey your masters according to the flesh with fear and trembling, in the sincerity of your heart, as Christ,
and not in service before the eyes, with partiality, as people-pleasers, but as slaves of Christ, doing the will of God from the heart;
serve with good sense, as the Lord and not man;
knowing that whatever good or evil each one does, that he will also receive from the Lord, whether he is slave or free.
and you masters, do likewise toward them, forgiving anger, knowing that your Lord and theirs is in heaven, and there is no partiality with him.
From now on, my brothers, be strong through the Lord and in the firmness of his might;
put on the whole armor of God, that you may be able to stand against those schemes of the devil,

for our struggle is not against blood and flesh, but against principalities and authorities, against the world-rulers of the darkness of this age, against the spirits of wickedness which are under heaven.
Therefore take up the whole armor of God, that you may be able to resist on that evil day, and do everything so that you may stand firm.
Stand firm then, gird your loins with truth, put on the coat of mail of righteousness.
and having shod your feet with the readiness of the gospel of peace.
In all things take up the shield of faith, with which you may be able to extinguish all the burning arrows of the evil one;
and put on the helmet of salvation, and take the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God.
With all prayer and supplication pray at every time in the Spirit, and likewise for this keep watch with all reverence and supplication for all the saints
and for me also, that utterance may be given to me in the opening of my mouth, to make known to you boldly the mystery of the gospel,
for which I am an ambassador in chains, so that in it I may declare myself openly, as it is fitting for me to speak.
And so that you also may know about me and what I am doing, Tychicus, the beloved brother and faithful servant in the Lord, will make everything known to you,
whom I have sent to you for this very purpose, so that you may know about us and that he may comfort your hearts.
Peace to the brothers, and love with faith, from God the Father and Jesus our Lord Jesus Christ.
Grace be with all who love our Lord Jesus Christ in incorruption. Amen.
